title: architecture(distribution): separate Cargo default features from selected release payload features
body:
Parent/controller: #5519 under #5518 and #5774.
Extends completed identity contract #4488 and final-payload authority #4521.

## Current verified premise

At `ripr-swarm/main` `8f29e0cfefe77488136ea1e3cf3ac4e269ca636b`, `policy/distribution.toml` schema 1.0 carries:

```toml
default_features = true
features = ["lang-python", "lang-rust", "lang-typescript"]
```

`xtask/src/policy/distribution/contract.rs` then requires `default_features = true`, hardcodes that exact feature set, and requires `crates/ripr/Cargo.toml`'s `[features].default` to equal it. The contract therefore conflates three different facts:

1. features available in the crate;
2. features selected for a particular native release payload;
3. features an ordinary `cargo install ripr` receives.

That was coherent while every release-selected language was a Cargo default. It cannot honestly represent an explicitly selected, initially non-default `lang-go` preview without either silently promoting Cargo defaults or weakening feature validation.

## One-PR outcome

Introduce one typed distribution-build contract that represents Cargo defaults and release selection independently while preserving exact effective-feature validation.

The accepted schema should carry the applicable equivalent of:

```text
crate available feature identities
Cargo build uses default features: yes/no
explicitly selected build features
normalized effective selected feature set
ordinary Cargo-install/default feature set
channel claim boundary
```

Exact field names belong to the implementation. There must still be one source of truth; do not create separate wheel/npm/archive feature lists.

## Required behavior

- Parse and validate a new schema generation with `deny_unknown_fields` and an explicit migration from 1.0.
- Derive the effective release feature set from the actual build-mode inputs; do not accept a desired effective list that disagrees with `--no-default-features` / `--features` semantics.
- Validate crate available/default feature identities separately from the selected release build.
- Preserve the current three-feature default build byte-for-byte in meaning when the migrated contract selects no extra feature.
- Make final-payload producer/receipt inputs capable of binding a non-default feature selection without claiming ordinary Cargo installation contains it.
- Expose enough typed state for Maturin/npm/archive consumers to use the same selection in later issues.
- Keep version, target, package names, payload identity and support tier outside this distinction unless already governed by the current contract.

## Discriminating controls

1. Current default build migrates and passes with the same effective three-feature set.
2. A contract selects one existing non-default feature through explicit build arguments and passes only when compiler-artifact features agree.
3. Metadata lists a feature but actual build arguments omit it -> fail.
4. `--no-default-features` is recorded while default features appear in the claimed effective set -> fail.
5. Actual compiler artifacts contain an unknown extra feature -> fail.
6. Duplicate, unknown, unavailable or misspelled features -> fail with the owning field named.
7. Cargo default features move without updating the ordinary-install contract -> fail.
8. Release-selected features move without invalidating payload identity -> fail.
9. A renderer or consumer reconstructing effective features independently makes a parity/architecture test fail.

## Acceptance

- [ ] one versioned typed contract separately represents crate defaults, release build selection and ordinary Cargo-install features;
- [ ] effective selected features are derived and compared with actual compiler-artifact evidence;
- [ ] archive, wheel and npm builders can consume the same typed selection without hardcoded copies;
- [ ] existing current-default release behavior remains accepted;
- [ ] non-default selection no longer requires a false Cargo-default claim;
- [ ] distribution policy/unit/negative tests, `cargo xtask check-release-targets`, generated/file policy and relevant release-server tests pass;
- [ ] docs explain the distinction without making a Go or support-tier claim.

## Non-goals

No `lang-go` selection in this PR, no Cargo default change, no analyzer/parser work, no package build, no installed journey, no release/version selection, no publication, and no support promotion.

## Claim boundary

Completion makes the release contract capable of expressing a non-default feature honestly. It does not establish that Go or any other feature is selected, qualified, enabled in a project, or available through ordinary Cargo installation.
